title: "Learn from measurements"
output: rmarkdown::html_document

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5,
  out.width = "100%",
  dpi = 144
)
library(suppose)
```

This example uses R's built-in `PlantGrowth` data to update a two-condition
normal model. It is retrospective: the outcomes are public, and the prior and
fixed measurement SD below are illustrative analyst choices. They are not
prospectively elicited beliefs.

## State the question and prior

Compare treatment 2 with control. R's dataset description does not supply physical
weight units, so the record uses “weight units” rather than inventing grams.

```{r prior}
belief <- claim(
  "Does treatment 2 increase mean dried weight by more than 0.5 weight units?",
  author = "Tutorial analyst",
  target = "Mean dried weight for trt2 minus ctrl",
  units = "weight units",
  threshold = 0.5,
  scope = "PlantGrowth; group codes 0 = ctrl and 1 = trt2",
  assumptions = "Independent normal measurements; SD fixed at 0.6 for illustration",
  unresolved = "Retrospective example; independence and causal meaning need justification"
)
judgments <- lapply(0:1, function(condition) {
  judgment(
    condition,
    c(4, 6),
    c(0.05, 0.95),
    units = "weight units",
    condition_units = "group code",
    author = "Tutorial analyst",
    answer = "Illustrative central 90% interval for the population mean: [4, 6]",
    source = "Analyst-selected tutorial prior",
    observed = "Public PlantGrowth outcomes already available"
  )
})
prior <- fit_prior(belief, judgments, correlation = 0, batch_sd = c(0.6, 0.6))
record <- record_revision(
  elicitation_record(belief),
  belief,
  prior,
  predict_prior(prior, seed = 47),
  reason = "Keep an explicitly illustrative prior for the retrospective example"
)
```

## Retain the measurements and their source

The observation format separates identity, condition, outcome, batch, specimen,
and observation time. Unknown times stay unknown. In this example each row is
assumed to represent a separate plant.

```{r measurements}
plants <- subset(datasets::PlantGrowth, group %in% c("ctrl", "trt2"))
ids <- paste0("plant-", seq_len(nrow(plants)))
rows <- data.frame(
  observation_id = ids,
  condition = as.character(plants$group),
  outcome = plants$weight,
  batch = ids,
  specimen = ids,
  observed_at = "unknown"
)
observations <- import_observations(
  rows,
  source = "R datasets::PlantGrowth; ctrl and trt2",
  protocol = "Published dried plant weights; independence assumed for tutorial",
  author = "Tutorial analyst",
  units = "weight units",
  role = "update",
  exposure = "explored"
)
record <- record_observations(
  record,
  observations,
  reason = "Retain published outcomes with explicit prior exposure"
)
```

Use a CSV path in place of `rows` for your own data. Missing outcomes remain in
the imported record. An explicit unit conversion uses `outcome * scale + offset`;
Suppose does not infer a conversion from a column name.

## Update under the stated model

Map the observed labels to the two conditions in the prior. Confirming
independence is a scientific assertion, not something this function establishes.

```{r update}
updated <- update_prior(
  prior,
  observations,
  condition_map = c(ctrl = 0, trt2 = 1),
  independent = TRUE
)
record <- record_update(
  record,
  updated,
  reason = "Retrospective update under fixed SD assumptions"
)
updated
```

```{r update-plot, fig.alt="Prior and posterior uncertainty for the PlantGrowth treatment contrast under an illustrative normal model with fixed measurement SDs."}
plot_update(updated)
```

The posterior conditions on both the measurements and the model. The fixed SD
of 0.6 is not estimated here. If uncertainty about measurement noise matters,
consider the separate [regression workflow](regression.html), which uses a new
prior specification and an unknown common variance.

## Check sensitivity

Vary prior strength and likelihood weight separately. Power 1 is the original
update. Here a change of 0.1 weight units or five percentage points is an
illustrative threshold for closer review.

```{r sensitivity}
sensitivity <- sensitivity_analysis(
  record,
  record$updates[[1]]$id,
  quantities = c("estimate", "probability"),
  estimate_change = 0.1,
  probability_change = 0.05
)
```

```{r sensitivity-plot, fig.alt="Changes in the posterior mean contrast as prior strength and likelihood weight are varied separately around the original model."}
plot_sensitivity(sensitivity)
```

This checks selected strength changes. It does not test alternative distribution
shapes, dependence assumptions, or measurement SDs. Retain a reviewed comparison
with `record_sensitivity()`.

## Keep exploration separate from a future check

These explored outcomes are not an independent prospective test. For future,
unseen outcomes, `commit_test()` freezes the model basis, planned measurement IDs,
protocol, deadline, and predictive interval. `assess_test()` later compares the
complete designated cohort against that original commitment.

Missing outcomes can leave an assessment awaiting data or inconclusive. A later
model revision does not rewrite the frozen prediction. The [methods guide](methods.html)
explains the interpretation and current restrictions of this check.
